idiom_name: Ktor Authentication plugin with named providers (basic/bearer/jwt/oauth) and provider() for custom schemes
implementation_notes: Ktor realizes the pattern as a plugin: install(Authentication) plus provider functions (basic, bearer, jwt, form, session) each configured with a validate or authenticate block that turns credentials into a Principal; authenticate("name") protects route subtrees and call.principal<T>() returns the typed principal, so the mechanism is chosen per route by provider name and provider("custom") adds new mechanisms. On Spring, the equivalent seam is AuthenticationProvider behind AuthenticationManager. Because providers are configuration inside the plugin, a hand-written abstract authenticator is unnecessary.
pitfalls: validate/authenticate blocks are suspend functions; blocking JDBC or LDAP calls inside them stall the event loop - move blocking work to a dispatcher.
Returning a principal of a type other than call.principal<T>() expects fails at runtime; prefer Ktor's typed authentication API, which binds the scheme to its principal type.
A provider that returns null when the identity provider is unreachable is indistinguishable from invalid credentials; distinguish 401 from 503.
AuthenticationStrategy semantics (Required, Optional, FirstSuccessful) decide whether nested providers must all pass; the default can differ from the intended policy.
